title: Save, revise and finalize a Training record
summary: Create a fictional record with the built-in Training form, verify a saved narrative revision and public attachment, finalize accurately, and inspect the first retained revision and record number.
prerequisites: Use an authorized account in a fictional practice department where Records is already usable; honor any normal access or Protected Data verification gate.
Use the built-in Training definition, a distinct software-only course/reference and a public plain-text handout; preserve other records and numbering settings.
For this software exercise leave participants and unit response times empty, and attest only to the activity actually documented.

sector_examples.Chicago Fire: Use a clearly labeled software orientation record with no fabricated attendance or response times; retain its draft identity and finalized revision.
sector_examples.Community care and mental health: Document an operational platform practice using fictional content and a public handout, without client histories or assessment claims.
sector_examples.Search and rescue: Keep software practice distinct from a mission response and preserve only actual participation/time data.
sector_examples.Security: Review a fictional platform-training entry and its signed version, preserving the record’s original identifiers.
sector_examples.Wildland: Document seasonal software familiarization with a truthful narrative and the actual saved revision rather than invented deployment activity.
sector_examples.Industrial response: Retain a system-training software example, public attachment and first finalized version without treating it as proof of physical drills or credentials.

scenes.title: Identify the built-in Training record form
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
scenes.narration: In Records, the New Record form has Training selected in Definition. This built-in form provides course information, a narrative, participant rows and optional unit times. Our fictional Chicago Fire exercise demonstrates the record lifecycle. It does not represent a physical training session or attendance. Enter a distinct Course, Training Only, Records Software Entry, followed by the exercise date. The Course code is Academy Rec Twenty-Nine, and External ID carries a separate exercise reference. Location says Fictional Software Workspace. Review Start and the empty End before continuing.
scenes.practice: On New Record, confirm Training is selected before preparing a distinctly named software exercise.
source_limits: Actual typed built-in Training form on New. No custom department definition is involved; changing Definition would reload a form. No initial New Record launcher click is pictured before this form.
Prepared fields only. Start initialized by normal form, End empty; Station/group dash later resolves to author group Command. No saved draft yet.

scenes.title: Describe only the activity that actually occurred
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
scenes.narration: The initial Narrative explains that this is a software record-entry exercise and that no physical training, attendance or operational response occurred. Write enough context for someone reading the record later. Below it, Participants provides a person selector, an optional assigned unit and a role. We leave the participant unselected. A blank chooser is not an attendance entry, and adding a name would make a different factual claim. The exercise therefore keeps this section empty.
scenes.practice: Write an explicit software-only narrative and leave the participant chooser empty.
source_limits: Initial software-only narrative and blank participant controls. This is not the later corrected narrative. Lower/right unit table clipped.

scenes.title: Keep optional unit response data truthful
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
scenes.narration: The Units section offers a checkbox for each unit and columns for Dispatched, En route, On scene, Released and In quarters. These fields belong to the record’s response data. They are not instructions to change a unit’s live status. We leave all unit selections and time entries untouched because no response happened. Review the displayed rows and preserve those empty selections rather than entering invented times to make a record appear complete.
scenes.practice: Inspect the unit/timestamp columns without selecting a unit or entering response times.

scenes.title: Edit the same draft instead of creating another
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
scenes.narration: Use Edit on this saved draft to revise its content. Continue with the existing record rather than opening another New Record form. The revised Narrative states that this is software record entry, no physical training or operational response occurred, and no personnel or unit times were added. Course, code and Location remain the exercise values. Read the complete text in the visible editor after typing; the content on screen must match the intended statement before you rely on it.

scenes.title: Verify the persisted narrative
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
scenes.narration: A fresh View Record readback now contains the corrected narrative on the same draft and the same reference. It remains Draft, with no final number. Checking a separate readback is valuable even when a draft supports automatic saving: text visible in an editor is not sufficient evidence that the intended version is stored. If the result is unexpected, inspect this existing draft before repeating a create action. Here the software-only revision is present and ready for the next step.
scenes.practice: Reopen View Record and compare the stored narrative and draft reference with your intended revision.
source_limits: Fresh readback proves corrected narrative stored on same own draft/reference. The exact later manual Edit Save button was not captured; do not relabel006as that later action or claim an observed autosave status.

scenes.title: Attest to the bounded software record and finalize
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
required_labels: I attest that this record is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge.
scenes.narration: Read the narrative and stored handout before signing. The attestation says the record is accurate and complete to the best of your knowledge. In this exercise, accuracy means accurately documenting a software practice with no physical training or response. Check the attestation and use Finalize. The fresh result shows Finalized and the actual issued number, T R N, Twenty Twenty-Six, Zero Zero Zero Two. The draft reference remains. Amend is now available for later corrections; a finalized revision is preserved rather than overwritten by ordinary draft editing.
scenes.practice: Review the software content and handout, then use the ordinary attestation and Finalize only when accurate.
source_limits: Own accurate software-only content and stored handout reviewed; attestation checked and normal Finalize visible before submission. No native dialog expected from this form.
Initial Finalized result TRN-2026-0002 with retained D-YXS93 and same recordID. Amend replaces Edit in header. This historical first-finalization state predates a separate later amendment exercise.

scenes.title: Use the same record discipline across sectors
scenes.capture_intent: Show actual typed Training record controls, saved readbacks and first-finalization revision in their retained causal order.
scenes.narration: Chicago Fire can use this pattern for a software orientation record. Community care and mental-health teams can document an operational software exercise without client histories. Search-and-rescue teams can keep practice documentation distinct from a mission response. Security teams can retain a fictional platform exercise; wildland coordinators can document seasonal software familiarization; industrial teams can preserve a system-training example and public handout. Across all six settings, use accurate narrative, actual participants and times only when they occurred, a verified attachment, and the saved revision that supports the statement being reviewed.
